blind.why: Tracer read: CS2 (t4_024) shows a long bright orange-white streak from barrel to target with a spark at the hit, so shot direction is obvious. Ours (g_fire_0, pip at 7.5m) has a nice muzzle star but the tracer is 2-3 faint grey dashes that vanish against the light wall.

Hit confirmation at range: CS2 (t2_029) has a tracer plus a big coloured mist at the hit point. Ours, 50ms after a body hit (g_fire_3), has no tracer and no burst at the hit point. Only the character's white flash shows anything happened.
Muzzle flash: our yellow star core with glow is crisp, short (2-3 frames) and sits low-right without hiding the crosshair. CS2's (t1_019) is richer but heavier. Readability goes to ours.

biggest_gap: Tracers are effectively invisible in real play. Own pip shots at 7.5m show as faint 1px grey dashes (shots/critic-vfx/g_fire_0-1.png). In vfx-lab, tracer-beam and tracer-comet are a barely visible dotted line or a dot (frames/tracer-beam_1.png). Even the 60-tracer 'fight' stress shows no streaks (l_fight_1.png). An enemy tracer vfx.tracer((4,1.4,-46)->(0.7,1.55,-29.5),0x2fd0ff,'arc'|'beam'), seen from the player at (0,0,-30), renders as one static ~3px grey dot with no cyan colour and no streak (h_in_*_0-1.png). CS2 tracers are thick, HDR-bright streaks with a hot white core, several metres long and visible for 2-4 frames, readable at 30m+ and when coming toward you. Fix: a minimum screen-space width of about 2-3px, a core brightness that survives bloom and tonemapping, length tied to speed so a streak is visible on at least 2 frames, a camera-facing ribbon so near-axial tracers still read, and team or tagger tint kept at full saturation.
other_gaps: Wall impacts on light surfaces are close to invisible: 8 pip shots at a sandstone pillar (g_wall_3-5, s_wallcrop.png) give a faint ring and a 3px puff, and no readable bullet-hole marks remain 1s later. CS2 leaves dark holes plus a surface-coloured dust or chip burst at every hit, so a spray can be read on the wall.

No hit burst on bodies at range: tag:hit has no spark or light-mist at the hit point, so it relies on the character flash alone. CS2's blood mist is the main 'I hit' cue at distance; use a stylised light burst in the tagger colour.

Clutter when effects stack: in the lab 'fight' stress, the stacked shatter floor glows wash out a white disc about 6m wide over the floor and targets (l_fight_1.png). The single tag-out floor shockwave at about 1.0s also covers about 40% of the lower screen at 7.5m (s_out.png frame 7). Cap the additive floor glow and lower its intensity per instance.
Lab tracer framing ('wide' cam) is too far to judge tracers, and the lab shooter is placed so tracers run nearly along the view axis.
Footstep dust is invisible at 1-4 frames (l_footstep_*). That is acceptable for CS2 parity, but then drop the cost. land-hard reads as a flat white disc rather than dust.
bugs: vfx.tracer() for an enemy shot passing 0.7m from the camera renders as a static ~3px grey dot, with no colour or streak (shots/critic-vfx/h_in_arc_0.png, h_in_beam_0.png).

muzzle-world in vfx-lab: the flash sits about 0.3m above and ahead of the dummy's gun tip and does not touch the barrel (shots/critic-vfx/frames/muzzle-world_0.png). Not verified on real character models.

CPU hitches inside vfx.update (swiftshader on a loaded host, so noisy): 10.7ms max over the window containing the first tag-out in game. In the lab, after the fight stress, 145.8ms max during the 2-8s window when 640 shards expire, and idle average stayed at 1.08ms against a 0.37ms baseline with 0 particles alive. Needs profiling on real hardware.
Not vfx (combat/viewmodel): calling combat.give(me,'arc') then switchTo(me,'arc') in live phase throws TypeError at src/combat/viewmodel/index.js:330 on the next advance.
strengths: Tag-out sequence (crown ping, then crystal tint, then confetti shard burst, then floor ring) is readable, well timed and satisfying (s_out.png).
Muzzle flash is crisp, short and does not hide the target.
Metal impact sparks and the stone puff have good easing and timing in the lab.
Batching is excellent: about 940 particles, 640 CPU shards and 60 tracers cost only +9 draw calls. In-game firing adds +5 calls.
